items.explanation: 71-year-old man (DOB 1955-08-23) with atrial fibrillation on the problem list and restated in every cardiology clinic note (most recent 2026-07-28). CHA2DS2-VASc 3: hypertension (Condition/a85598ce-8a90-5b39-a580-ac8bd7329014), age 65-74, vascular disease (coronary atherosclerosis of native coronary artery, Condition/75b86cdb-2074-5574-a9b2-2384b54ee4f0). Score >=2 in a man means guideline-recommended oral anticoagulation, yet the only current medication order is tamsulosin 0.4 mg daily; no anticoagulant order is active at 2026-09-24 and the clinic notes list no anticoagulant. Needs review for starting an oral anticoagulant (the 2025 hemorrhage complicating a procedure should be weighed).

Citalopram 40 mg daily (QT watch list) was started at the cardiology clinic visit on 2026-03-02 (first citalopram order, and first appearance in the clinic medication list that day). Because the start is on/after 2026-03-01 the revised memo applies: ECG within 14 days, i.e. by 2026-03-16. ECG 104882441 was recorded on 2026-03-07, five days after the start, so the requirement was met (QTc 371 ms, normal).

Amiodarone 200 mg daily (QT watch list) was started at the cardiology clinic visit of 2025-11-10 (first outpatient amiodarone order; earlier amiodarone was inpatient in January 2025 and had stopped). The start is on/after 2025-09-01 but before 2026-03-01, so the original 30-day window applies: ECG due by 2025-12-10. ECG 106885519 was obtained 2025-11-24, 14 days after the start, so the monitoring requirement was met - although that ECG showed QTc 520 ms, which is handled as a separate QT_SAFETY item.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch list) was started at the cardiology clinic visit of 2026-02-12. The start is before 2026-03-01, so the earlier memo's 30-day window is kept: ECG due by 2026-03-14. ECG 101538691 was recorded 2026-03-08, 24 days after the start - within 30 days, so completed (sinus rhythm, QTc 396 ms).

Escitalopram 10 mg daily was started at the cardiology clinic visit of 2026-08-01 (first appearance in the clinic medication list that day; the December 2025 escitalopram order was a brief inpatient course that had stopped). Start on/after 2026-03-01, so an ECG was required within 14 days, by 2026-08-15. The only ECG in the chart is 106035722 from 2025-12-25, before the start, and no ECG has been obtained since. The requirement is overdue as of 2026-09-24.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily was started at the cardiology clinic visit of 2026-04-10. Because the start is on/after 2026-03-01 the revised memo applies and an ECG was required within 14 days, by 2026-04-24. The only ECG in the chart, 107859369, was recorded 2026-04-29 - 19 days after the start, outside the 14-day window (it would have satisfied the superseded 30-day rule). The requirement was therefore not met within the required time and is overdue; the late tracing itself was unremarkable (sinus rhythm, QTc 377 ms).

Haloperidol 2 mg twice daily (QT watch list) was started at the cardiology clinic visit of 2026-09-15 (earlier haloperidol was parenteral during the February-March 2025 admission). Start on/after 2026-03-01, so an ECG is required within 14 days, by 2026-09-29. No ECG has been obtained yet (last tracing 104253928, 2025-03-09), but the deadline falls after the 2026-09-24 evaluation date, so the requirement is not yet due; the ECG should be arranged in the next few days.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily was started at the cardiology clinic visit of 2026-08-10, so under the revised memo an ECG was required within 14 days, by 2026-08-24. No ECG for this patient exists in the chart, but the nurse telephone note of 2026-08-25 (DocumentReference/5e12a8aa-0439-53cd-a194-cc1a277d296d) records that the patient had an ECG at Northside Urgent Care on 2026-08-18 - within the window - and that the report was requested by fax but has not been received. That outside tracing could have satisfied the requirement, so completion cannot be determined until the report arrives.

At the cardiology clinic visit of 2026-09-01 Dr Kessler documented INR 1.6, subtherapeutic, and increased warfarin from 5 mg to 7.5 mg daily with a plan to recheck. Under the 2026-03-01 memo an INR was required within 7 days, by 2026-09-08. INR 2.3 was resulted on 2026-09-05 (Observation/d6b3bad5-3076-5e66-b42f-6d1705a1bb9e), four days after the change, so the requirement was met.

On 2026-09-10 the clinic pharmacist (L. Nguyen, PharmD, acting under the anticoagulation standing order) documented a home INR of 3.4 and decreased warfarin from 5 mg to 4 mg daily. Under the 2026-03-01 memo an INR was required within 7 days, by 2026-09-17. The most recent INR in the chart is 2.6 from 2026-08-22, before the change, and no INR has been drawn since; the requirement is overdue as of 2026-09-24.

71-year-old woman (DOB 1955-09-07) with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation (Condition/66dd1300-261e-52a9-8985-0b6d72a35db9). CHA2DS2-VASc 5: prior ischaemic stroke = 2 (cerebral infarction due to embolism, Condition/e810ff58-1fb4-5a1e-85e7-faa301f89b61, with residual hemiplegia), hypertension = 1 (Condition/ee66ac4a-6c51-5922-a92b-94575e18064e), age 65-74 = 1, female = 1. Score >=3 in a woman (and secondary stroke prevention) means anticoagulation is recommended, but current orders are only carvedilol, metoprolol and famotidine - no anticoagulant is active at 2026-09-24. Her most recent ECG (102298909, 2025-03-14) shows sinus rhythm, which does not remove the indication in paroxysmal AF. Bleeding risk (thrombocytopenia, history of falls, non-ruptured cerebral aneurysm) should be weighed at review.

Apixaban 5 mg twice daily is currently ordered (MedicationRequest/dc397aff-c600-5fef-bb34-0b71ebfe70b2, 2026-08-20, valid to 2026-12-28). The outside-records summary of 2026-08-12 documents an admission 2026-08-02 to 2026-08-05 for upper GI bleeding from a duodenal ulcer with haemoglobin nadir 6.9 and 2 units transfused, and states that apixaban was held at discharge pending cardiology review. The anticoagulant was nevertheless re-ordered on 2026-08-20 and no cardiology review of the bleed is documented; concurrent clopidogrel and aspirin add further bleeding risk. Continuation needs prescriber review.

Two direct oral anticoagulants are simultaneously current: apixaban 5 mg twice daily (MedicationRequest/7206d5b5-544c-54e3-b118-d3a669f020a7, 2026-07-15 to 2026-12-26) and rivaroxaban 20 mg daily (MedicationRequest/b71a461f-9f14-5217-a3bb-3c242d0d08eb, 2026-07-15 to 2026-12-25). The 2026-07-15 cardiology note states the intent was to switch from rivaroxaban to apixaban for insurance coverage, but the rivaroxaban order was never stopped, so both remain active at 2026-09-24. Overlapping anticoagulants carry a major bleeding risk and one order must be discontinued.

The cardiology note of 2026-06-10 10:55 states 'ECG obtained today: normal sinus rhythm, rate 72'. Both ECGs recorded that same day contradict it: 107914094 (2026-06-10 17:13) and 103088543 (2026-06-10 19:36) each show an irregularly irregular narrow-complex rhythm with no organised P waves at a mean ventricular rate of 139 and 144 bpm - atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response, not sinus rhythm at 72. The discrepancy affects rate-control and anticoagulation decisions and needs clarification.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily is a QT watch-list drug and is currently ordered (MedicationRequest/8de890c6, 2026-04-23 to 2027-01-02). The patient's most recent ECG (108018814, 2023-10-08) is sinus rhythm at 68 bpm with QT 472 ms and Bazett QTc 505 ms, at or above the 500 ms threshold in the QT monitoring memo, and up 150 ms from the prior tracing (100065910, QTc 354 ms). Most recent electrolytes are normal (K 4.1 mEq/L and Mg 2.1 mg/dL, both 2025-08-23), so they do not explain the prolongation. Prescriber review required; a repeat ECG is also reasonable as the last tracing is nearly three years old.

Amiodarone 200 mg daily (watch-list drug) is currently ordered (MedicationRequest/1014aca9, 2026-07-29 to 2027-01-05) and has been continuous since it was started at the 2025-11-10 clinic visit. The most recent ECG (106885519, 2025-11-24) shows sinus rhythm at 62 bpm with QT 512 ms and Bazett QTc 520 ms, above the 500 ms threshold, and 108 ms longer than the preceding tracing (108780865, QTc 412 ms). Potassium 4.4 mEq/L and magnesium 2.2 mg/dL (2026-04-20) are normal. Prescriber review of amiodarone dosing and a repeat ECG are needed.

Citalopram 40 mg daily (watch-list drug, and above the 20 mg/day dose advised in older adults) is currently ordered (MedicationRequest/7f787d30, 2026-05-29 to 2026-12-25). The most recent ECG (104821039, 2023-11-10) is sinus rhythm at 70 bpm with QT 484 ms and Bazett QTc 523 ms, above the 500 ms threshold and 119 ms longer than the prior tracing (107149156, QTc 404 ms). Most recent potassium 4.5 mEq/L (2026-01-21) and magnesium 2.1 mg/dL (2023-12-01) are normal. Prescriber review of citalopram dose plus a current ECG and electrolytes are needed.

Amiodarone 200 mg daily (watch-list drug) is currently ordered (MedicationRequest/c6f532e9, 2026-08-22 to 2027-01-05). The most recent ECG (101515306, 2022-04-27) shows sinus bradycardia at 58 bpm with QT about 554 ms and Bazett QTc about 540 ms, well above the 500 ms threshold and 106 ms longer than the prior tracing (100867733, atrial fibrillation, QTc 434 ms). Potassium 4.1 mEq/L and magnesium 1.8 mg/dL (2026-02-14) are normal-low. She is 95 years old and also on metoprolol, so bradycardia compounds the risk. Prescriber review of amiodarone and a current ECG are needed.

interpretations.explanation: Sinus bradycardia at 53 bpm, RR regular (1092-1176 ms). Upright P before every QRS in II/aVF, PR 164 ms. Narrow QRS 84 ms with no bundle branch pattern; frontal axis -14 degrees (net QRS positive in I, slightly negative in aVF) = normal. QT 376 ms, Bazett QTc 353 ms at RR 1136 ms. Versus the prior tracing 108651109 (2018-12-13, sinus 66 bpm, PR 186 ms, QRS 88 ms, QTc 381 ms): rate slower, no rhythm, conduction or QTc change (QTc -28 ms).

Sinus rhythm at 68 bpm, regular (RR 880 ms). Upright P in II/aVF with a deep negative component in V1, PR about 135 ms. QRS 82 ms, axis +38 degrees = normal, no bundle branch block. Repolarisation is markedly prolonged with a broad late T wave: QT about 475 ms, Bazett QTc about 505 ms - at the QT watch-list threshold on escitalopram (separate QT_SAFETY item). Prior tracing 100065910 (2022-11-23, sinus 74 bpm, PR 120 ms, QRS 82 ms, QTc 354 ms): QTc has risen about 150 ms, so QTC_INCREASE_60 is flagged; rhythm and conduction unchanged.

Sinus rhythm at 70 bpm (RR 850 ms, minor sinus variation). Low-amplitude upright P in II/aVF before each QRS, PR about 155 ms. QRS 90 ms, axis +39 degrees = normal, no bundle branch block. Long, flat, low-amplitude T wave with QT about 484 ms and Bazett QTc about 523 ms on citalopram 40 mg daily (separate QT_SAFETY item). Prior tracing 107149156 (2020-06-17, sinus tachycardia 132 bpm, QRS 84 ms, QTc 404 ms): QTc up about 119 ms, so QTC_INCREASE_60; rhythm and conduction unchanged.

Sinus tachycardia at 121 bpm, RR regular (496 ms), with a small upright P in II/aVF before each QRS, PR about 130 ms. QRS 72 ms, axis +63 degrees = normal, no bundle branch block. QT about 282 ms, Bazett QTc about 400 ms. This is the only ECG in the chart, so there is no prior tracing for comparison.

Sinus tachycardia at 110 bpm; RR shortens smoothly from 570 to 540 ms. Small upright P in II/aVF (peak about 130 ms before the QRS) with PR about 120 ms and some PR-segment depression. QRS 82 ms, axis +45 degrees = normal, no bundle branch block. QT about 328 ms, Bazett QTc about 443 ms. Only ECG in the chart - no prior tracing.

Sinus rhythm at 97 bpm, regular (RR 616 ms). Prominent upright P in II/III/aVF, negative in V1, ending just before the QRS; PR about 118 ms. QRS 68 ms with tall R in V5 and net QRS positive in I and isoelectric in aVF: frontal axis about 0 degrees = normal. No bundle branch block. QT about 304 ms, QTc 387 ms. Only ECG in the chart - no prior tracing.

Sinus rhythm at 61 bpm (RR 984 ms after the first two longer cycles). Upright P in II/aVF peaking about 240 ms before the QRS with P onset about 275 ms and QRS onset about 60 ms before the R peak: PR about 212 ms, i.e. first-degree AV block. QRS is broad at 126 ms with a wide monophasic R in I and V6 peaking late and a deep broad QS in V1-V2 - left bundle branch block. Frontal axis -23 degrees = normal (borderline leftward). QT about 430 ms, QTc 433 ms. Prior tracing 103686933 (2024-06-03) shows the same LBBB (QRS 126 ms), PR about 208 ms and QTc 442 ms, so there is no new bundle branch block and no QTc change.

Atrial fibrillation with a mean ventricular rate of 99 bpm: RR intervals are chaotically irregular (386-1070 ms, coefficient of variation 0.29) and the averaged beat shows no organised P wave (peak pre-QRS amplitude only 0.01 mV in lead II), so no PR interval is measurable. QRS 74 ms, no bundle branch block. Frontal axis -63 degrees (QRS positive in I, negative in II and aVF) = left axis deviation. QT about 312 ms, Bazett QTc about 401 ms. Only ECG in the chart - no prior tracing. He is anticoagulated with warfarin.

Sinus bradycardia at 52 bpm, RR very regular (1160 ms), with a low-amplitude upright P in II/aVF and PR about 166 ms. QRS 86 ms, axis +34 degrees = normal, no bundle branch block. Tall T waves; QT about 404 ms, Bazett QTc 375 ms. Prior tracing 104629882 (2023-05-22) was also sinus at 57 bpm with a single premature beat and compensatory pause (QTc 345 ms), so no rhythm, conduction or QTc change.

Atrial fibrillation with a slow, irregular ventricular response, mean rate 53 bpm: RR intervals vary from 696 to 1164 ms with no repeating pattern and the averaged beat has essentially no atrial deflection (0.04 mV in lead II, versus 0.34 mV on the previous tracing), so no PR interval can be measured. QRS 82 ms, axis +25 degrees = normal, no bundle branch block. QT about 416 ms, Bazett QTc 392 ms. The prior tracing 107873952 (2024-11-12) was sinus rhythm at 69 bpm with a clear P wave and PR 166 ms (QTc 388 ms), so this is NEW_AF. She is anticoagulated with apixaban.

Sinus tachycardia at 121 bpm, RR very regular (494 ms), with an upright P in I/II before each QRS and PR about 130 ms. The QRS is now narrow at 84 ms with no terminal R in V1; frontal axis +139 degrees (net QRS negative in I, positive in aVF) = right axis deviation. QT about 292 ms, Bazett QTc about 418 ms. The prior tracing 106516875, recorded 13 hours earlier the same day (2024-12-05 01:33), showed a broad QRS of about 140 ms with a tall late R in V1 and wide S in I and V6, i.e. right bundle branch block (his documented Condition), with QTc about 460 ms. The intraventricular conduction delay has resolved on this tracing: RESOLVED_BUNDLE_BRANCH_BLOCK. QTc fell about 44 ms, below the 60 ms threshold.

Sinus rhythm at 77 bpm, regular (RR 783 ms), clear upright P waves in II/aVF with PR 148 ms. QRS 66 ms, axis +60 degrees = normal, no bundle branch block. QT about 380 ms, QTc about 425 ms. The prior tracing 109048192 (2020-02-02) was also sinus (with one interpolated premature beat producing an apparently irregular RR sequence) but had a long, low-amplitude, late T wave giving QT about 480 ms and QTc about 520 ms; QTc has fallen by roughly 95 ms, so QTC_DECREASE_60 is flagged. No change in rhythm or conduction.

Sinus rhythm at 74 bpm, regular (RR 812 ms). Upright P in I/II/aVF with PR about 178 ms. QRS 82 ms, axis +58 degrees = normal, no bundle branch block. QT about 374 ms, Bazett QTc 415 ms. Only ECG in the chart - no prior tracing.

Sinus bradycardia at 58 bpm with mild sinus variation (RR 984-1064 ms). Prominent upright P in II/III/aVF, PR about 108 ms. QRS 80 ms, axis +58 degrees = normal, no bundle branch block. Inverted T waves in V2-V3; QT about 422 ms, Bazett QTc 416 ms. Prior tracing 106045460 (2025-03-08, sinus 62 bpm, PR 108 ms, QRS 80 ms, QTc 444 ms): no rhythm, conduction or QTc change (QTc -28 ms). Haloperidol was started on 2026-09-15, after this ECG, so a follow-up tracing is required.

Sinus rhythm at 61 bpm. The underlying RR is regular at about 980 ms with a single premature beat (RR 538 ms) and a compensatory pause (1372 ms); apart from that couplet the rhythm is regular with an upright P in I/II before each QRS and PR about 194 ms (upper normal, not first-degree AV block). QRS 94 ms, no bundle branch pattern. Frontal axis -33 degrees (QRS positive in I, negative in II and aVF) = left axis deviation. QT about 376 ms, Bazett QTc 380 ms. This is the only ECG in the chart, so there is no prior tracing. Sinus rhythm on this tracing does not exclude her documented paroxysmal atrial fibrillation (see the anticoagulation item).

Sinus tachycardia at 102 bpm, RR regular (589 ms), upright P in II/aVF with PR about 134 ms. QRS 84 ms, axis +44 degrees = normal, no bundle branch block. Inverted T waves in V2-V3; QT about 338 ms, Bazett QTc 440 ms. Prior tracing 101016166 (2025-03-18, sinus 102 bpm, PR 126 ms, QRS 80 ms, QTc 437 ms): unchanged.

Sinus rhythm at 82 bpm, regular (RR 728 ms). Upright P in II/III/aVF peaking about 165 ms before the QRS, PR about 147 ms. QRS 88 ms with a small initial slur but no bundle branch pattern. Frontal axis +28 degrees = normal. QT about 346 ms, Bazett QTc about 412 ms. Only ECG in the chart - no prior tracing.

Sinus bradycardia at 54 bpm, RR regular (1100 ms). A well-formed upright P in II/III/aVF runs from about 252 ms to 165 ms before the QRS, followed by a flat, isoelectric PR segment to a QRS onset about 36 ms before the R peak: PR about 214 ms, i.e. first-degree AV block (his earlier tracings measured 178-196 ms). QRS 78 ms with very tall precordial R waves, no bundle branch block. Frontal axis +11 degrees = normal. QT about 392 ms, Bazett QTc 373 ms. Prior tracing 103042067 (2024-11-30, sinus 51 bpm, PR 182 ms, QRS 82 ms, QTc 356 ms): no bundle branch block change and no QTc change; the PR has lengthened past 200 ms, which is not one of the tracked change categories.

Sinus tachycardia at 104 bpm, RR regular (578 ms). Upright P in I/II/aVF (deeply negative in V1) from about 200 ms before the QRS, PR about 148 ms. QRS 88 ms, axis +22 degrees = normal, no bundle branch block. Widespread ST depression with a discrete T wave peaking at 190 ms that returns to baseline by about 275 ms: QT about 328 ms, Bazett QTc about 430 ms. Prior tracing 100698634 (2025-06-20) was sinus tachycardia at 147 bpm where T and P waves merge; QTc there is about 460 ms, so the change is under the 60 ms threshold. No rhythm or conduction change.

Regular rhythm at 69 bpm (RR 872 ms) that is not sinus: the atrial wave preceding each QRS is inverted in II, III and aVF and upright in I and aVL (peak about 130 ms before the QRS), indicating a low/ectopic atrial or coronary-sinus focus rather than sinus node origin. Atrioventricular conduction is 1:1 with a fixed PR of about 145 ms. QRS 76 ms with a very dominant R in I and aVL, no bundle branch block; net QRS area gives a frontal axis of about -25 degrees = normal (borderline leftward). QT about 392 ms, Bazett QTc about 420 ms. The prior tracing 104232242 (2025-04-27) showed the same non-sinus atrial activation at 60 bpm with QTc about 400 ms; no atrial fibrillation, flutter, paced rhythm, bundle branch block or QTc change.

Sinus rhythm at 83 bpm, RR very regular (720 ms). Upright P in II/aVF with PR about 146 ms. Narrow QRS 62 ms, axis +53 degrees = normal, no bundle branch block. QT about 332 ms, Bazett QTc 391 ms. Only ECG in the chart - no prior tracing.

Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response, mean rate 152 bpm: RR intervals are irregularly irregular (288-580 ms, coefficient of variation 0.19) and no organised P wave is present in the averaged beat, so no PR interval can be measured. QRS 68 ms, axis about -1 degree = normal, no bundle branch block. QT about 250 ms, Bazett QTc about 398 ms. The prior tracing 107374881 (2025-09-12) was sinus rhythm at 77 bpm with a discrete P wave, PR about 145 ms and one premature beat (QTc 405 ms), so this is NEW_AF. He is anticoagulated with apixaban.

Sinus tachycardia at 121 bpm, RR very regular (494-504 ms). One upright P per QRS in II/III/aVF, with the P onset partly merged into the preceding T wave; PR about 200 ms (upper limit of normal, not called first-degree AV block). QRS 84 ms, axis +46 degrees = normal, no bundle branch block. QT about 290 ms, QTc about 397 ms. Prior tracing 106186980 (2016-09-16, sinus 108 bpm, PR 168 ms, QRS 84 ms, QTc 394 ms): no rhythm, conduction or QTc change.

Sinus rhythm at 66 bpm, regular (RR 910 ms). Upright P in II/aVF, PR about 152 ms. QRS 84 ms, no bundle branch block. Frontal axis -29 degrees = normal (borderline leftward). QT about 368 ms, Bazett QTc 386 ms. Only ECG in the chart - no prior tracing.

Sinus rhythm at 73 bpm with mild sinus variation (RR 760-880 ms). Upright P in II/aVF (negative in V1) with PR about 164 ms. QRS 84 ms, axis +5 degrees = normal, no bundle branch block. QT about 350 ms, Bazett QTc 387 ms - consistent with the same-day clinic note documenting sinus rhythm. Prior tracing 105362569 (2025-11-21, two days earlier) was also sinus at 67 bpm but with ST depression and a long late T wave: QT about 488 ms, QTc about 517 ms. QTc has fallen about 130 ms, so QTC_DECREASE_60 is flagged; no rhythm or conduction change.

Sinus rhythm at 62 bpm, RR regular (970 ms). Low-amplitude but consistent upright P in II/aVF (this patient's P waves are small on all of his tracings), PR about 140 ms. QRS 90 ms, axis +64 degrees = normal, no bundle branch block. Repolarisation is prolonged with a broad T wave peaking at 385 ms: QT about 512 ms, Bazett QTc about 520 ms on amiodarone (separate QT_SAFETY item). Prior tracing 108780865 (2025-06-07) was sinus bradycardia at 47 bpm with marked sinus variation and QTc about 412 ms, so QTc has risen about 108 ms: QTC_INCREASE_60. No rhythm or conduction change.

Sinus rhythm at 72 bpm, regular (RR 832 ms). Upright P in I/II/aVF with PR about 138 ms. QRS 76 ms, axis +22 degrees = normal, no bundle branch block. QT about 350 ms, Bazett QTc 384 ms. Only ECG in the chart - no prior tracing. Note this tracing predates the escitalopram start of 2026-08-01, for which a post-start ECG is still outstanding.

Sinus rhythm at 81 bpm with physiological sinus variation (RR 656-856 ms in a smooth respiratory pattern). A clear upright P wave in II/III/aVF precedes every QRS (P onset about 208 ms, peak about 150 ms before the QRS), PR about 178 ms. QRS 74 ms, axis +39 degrees = normal, no bundle branch block. QT about 320 ms, Bazett QTc 371 ms. This confirms the same-day clinic note that the ECG showed sinus rhythm. Only ECG in the chart - no prior tracing.

Sinus rhythm at 68 bpm, regular (RR 882 ms). Upright P in II/III/aVF (negative in V1), PR about 140 ms. QRS 80 ms, axis +45 degrees = normal, no bundle branch block. QT about 372 ms, Bazett QTc 396 ms - normal, which satisfies the post-escitalopram monitoring ECG. No prior tracing in the chart.

Sinus rhythm at 69 bpm, regular (RR 864 ms), with a consistent low-amplitude atrial deflection before each QRS and PR about 145 ms. QRS 86 ms, no bundle branch pattern. QT about 350 ms, Bazett QTc 377 ms. As recorded, the net QRS area is strongly negative in lead I (-15.3 mV.ms) and slightly negative in aVF (-2.4 mV.ms), giving a frontal axis of about -171 degrees, i.e. extreme axis deviation, which is what is reported. Note however that the limb leads are markedly discordant - P, QRS and T all deeply negative in I and II with positive deflections in III and an upright QRS in aVR - while the precordial leads show normal R-wave progression; this is the pattern of right/left arm electrode reversal, and after correcting for it the frontal axis would be about -10 degrees (normal). Repeat with correct electrode placement is advised. Only ECG in the chart - no prior tracing.

Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response, mean rate 144 bpm: RR intervals are irregularly irregular (348-650 ms, coefficient of variation 0.16), the baseline is fibrillatory and no organised P wave is present, so no PR interval can be measured. QRS 86 ms, axis +6 degrees = normal, no bundle branch block. QT about 288 ms, Bazett QTc about 447 ms. The prior tracing 107914094 was recorded 2 hours 23 minutes earlier the same day and shows the same atrial fibrillation at 139 bpm (QTc about 441 ms), so there is no change. Both tracings contradict the same-day note describing normal sinus rhythm at 72 bpm (see the CONTRADICTION item). She is anticoagulated with warfarin.

Sinus tachycardia at 101 bpm, regular (RR 592 ms), upright P in II/aVF with PR 142 ms. QRS 84 ms, axis +51 degrees = normal, no bundle branch block. QT about 312 ms, QTc 402 ms. The prior tracing 102910502 was recorded 34 seconds earlier the same morning and is essentially identical (sinus 101 bpm, PR 140 ms, QRS 82 ms, QTc 401 ms) - no changes.

Sinus bradycardia at 58 bpm; RR drifts smoothly from 1100 to 975 ms and a low-amplitude but consistent upright P precedes every QRS in II/III/aVF (peak about 200 ms before the QRS), PR about 190 ms. QRS 84 ms, axis +33 degrees = normal, no bundle branch block. Marked repolarisation prolongation: QT about 554 ms, Bazett QTc about 540 ms, on amiodarone (see the QT_SAFETY item). The prior tracing 100867733 (2022-04-06) showed atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response (mean 131 bpm, RR 324-616 ms, no P waves, QTc 434 ms), so sinus rhythm has been restored (RESOLVED_AF) and QTc has risen by about 106 ms (QTC_INCREASE_60).

Sinus tachycardia at 107 bpm, RR very regular (554-564 ms). Broad, slightly notched upright P in II/III/aVF ending just before the QRS; PR about 180 ms. QRS 66 ms, axis +52 degrees = normal, no bundle branch block. QT about 326 ms, QTc about 430 ms. Prior tracing 107274479 (2019-07-27, sinus 75 bpm, PR 150 ms, QRS 66 ms, QTc 411 ms): faster rate only, no rhythm, conduction or QTc change.

Regular narrow-complex tachycardia at 141 bpm (RR 404-454 ms, CV 0.02). Two low-amplitude atrial waves of identical inferior vector (positive II/III/aVF, negative I, positive V1) recur every 210-215 ms - one in the early ST segment about 85 ms after the QRS and one about 155 ms before the next QRS - giving an atrial rate near 280/min with 2:1 conduction, i.e. atrial flutter rather than sinus tachycardia; there is no isoelectric baseline and no PR interval can be measured, so pr_ms is null. The atrial wave vector also differs from this patient's documented sinus P wave (ECG 105224815, 2022-07-08). QRS 80 ms, axis 0 degrees = normal, no bundle branch block; QT about 274 ms, QTc about 420 ms. The prior tracing 109839112 (2022-07-11) showed atrial fibrillation (mean 110 bpm, RR 380-822 ms, no organised atrial activity, QTc 428 ms), so the rhythm has organised into flutter: NEW_ATRIAL_FLUTTER and RESOLVED_AF. Atrial flutter documented in the problem list (Condition I48.92) supports this reading; a pacemaker is present but the rhythm is not paced.

Sinus rhythm at 91 bpm, regular (RR 660 ms), upright P in II/aVF with negative component in V1; PR about 140 ms. QRS 76 ms, no bundle branch block. arguments.explanation: Regular narrow-complex tachycardia at 141 bpm (RR 404-454 ms, CV 0.02). Two low-amplitude atrial waves of identical inferior vector (positive II/III/aVF, negative I, positive V1) recur every 210-215 ms - one in the early ST segment about 85 ms after the QRS and one about 155 ms before the next QRS - giving an atrial rate near 280/min with 2:1 conduction, i.e. atrial flutter rather than sinus tachycardia; there is no isoelectric baseline and no PR interval can be measured, so pr_ms is null. The atrial wave vector also differs from this patient's documented sinus P wave (ECG 105224815, 2022-07-08). QRS 80 ms, axis 0 degrees = normal, no bundle branch block; QT about 274 ms, QTc about 420 ms. The prior tracing 109839112 (2022-07-11) showed atrial fibrillation (mean 110 bpm, RR 380-822 ms, no organised atrial activity, QTc 428 ms), so the rhythm has organised into flutter: NEW_ATRIAL_FLUTTER and RESOLVED_AF. Atrial flutter documented in the problem list (Condition I48.92) supports this reading; a pacemaker is present but the rhythm is not paced.

Regular narrow-complex tachycardia at 141 bpm (RR 404-454 ms, CV 0.02). Two low-amplitude atrial waves of identical inferior vector (positive II/III/aVF, negative I, positive V1) recur every 210-215 ms - one in the early ST segment about 85 ms after the QRS and one about 155 ms before the next QRS - giving an atrial rate near 280/min with 2:1 conduction, i.e. atrial flutter rather than sinus tachycardia; there is no isoelectric baseline and no PR interval can be measured, so pr_ms is null. The atrial wave vector also differs from this patient's documented sinus P wave (ECG 105224815, 2022-07-08). QRS 80 ms, axis 0 degrees = normal, no bundle branch block; QT about 274 ms, QTc about 420 ms. The prior tracing 109839112 (2022-07-11) showed atrial fibrillation (mean 110 bpm, RR 380-822 ms, no organised atrial activity, QTc 428 ms), so the rhythm has organised into flutter: NEW_ATRIAL_FLUTTER and RESOLVED_AF. interpretations.explanation: Sinus bradycardia at 53 bpm, RR regular (1092-1176 ms). Upright P before every QRS in II/aVF, PR 164 ms. Narrow QRS 84 ms with no bundle branch pattern; frontal axis -14 degrees (net QRS positive in I, slightly negative in aVF) = normal. QT 376 ms, Bazett QTc 353 ms at RR 1136 ms. Versus the prior tracing 108651109 (2018-12-13, sinus 66 bpm, PR 186 ms, QRS 88 ms, QTc 381 ms): rate slower, no rhythm, conduction or QTc change (QTc -28 ms).

Sinus rhythm at 68 bpm, regular (RR 880 ms). Upright P in II/aVF with a deep negative component in V1, PR about 135 ms. QRS 82 ms, axis +38 degrees = normal, no bundle branch block. Repolarisation is markedly prolonged with a broad late T wave: QT about 475 ms, Bazett QTc about 505 ms - at the QT watch-list threshold on escitalopram (separate QT_SAFETY item). Prior tracing 100065910 (2022-11-23, sinus 74 bpm, PR 120 ms, QRS 82 ms, QTc 354 ms): QTc has risen about 150 ms, so QTC_INCREASE_60 is flagged; rhythm and conduction unchanged.

Sinus rhythm at 70 bpm (RR 850 ms, minor sinus variation). Low-amplitude upright P in II/aVF before each QRS, PR about 155 ms. QRS 90 ms, axis +39 degrees = normal, no bundle branch block. Long, flat, low-amplitude T wave with QT about 484 ms and Bazett QTc about 523 ms on citalopram 40 mg daily (separate QT_SAFETY item). Prior tracing 107149156 (2020-06-17, sinus tachycardia 132 bpm, QRS 84 ms, QTc 404 ms): QTc up about 119 ms, so QTC_INCREASE_60; rhythm and conduction unchanged.

Sinus tachycardia at 121 bpm, RR regular (496 ms), with a small upright P in II/aVF before each QRS, PR about 130 ms. QRS 72 ms, axis +63 degrees = normal, no bundle branch block. QT about 282 ms, Bazett QTc about 400 ms. This is the only ECG in the chart, so there is no prior tracing for comparison.

Sinus tachycardia at 110 bpm; RR shortens smoothly from 570 to 540 ms. Small upright P in II/aVF (peak about 130 ms before the QRS) with PR about 120 ms and some PR-segment depression. QRS 82 ms, axis +45 degrees = normal, no bundle branch block. QT about 328 ms, Bazett QTc about 443 ms. Only ECG in the chart - no prior tracing.

Sinus rhythm at 97 bpm, regular (RR 616 ms). Prominent upright P in II/III/aVF, negative in V1, ending just before the QRS; PR about 118 ms. QRS 68 ms with tall R in V5 and net QRS positive in I and isoelectric in aVF: frontal axis about 0 degrees = normal. No bundle branch block. QT about 304 ms, QTc 387 ms. Only ECG in the chart - no prior tracing.

Sinus rhythm at 61 bpm (RR 984 ms after the first two longer cycles). Upright P in II/aVF peaking about 240 ms before the QRS with P onset about 275 ms and QRS onset about 60 ms before the R peak: PR about 212 ms, i.e. first-degree AV block. QRS is broad at 126 ms with a wide monophasic R in I and V6 peaking late and a deep broad QS in V1-V2 - left bundle branch block. Frontal axis -23 degrees = normal (borderline leftward). QT about 430 ms, QTc 433 ms. Prior tracing 103686933 (2024-06-03) shows the same LBBB (QRS 126 ms), PR about 208 ms and QTc 442 ms, so there is no new bundle branch block and no QTc change.

Sinus rhythm at 77 bpm, regular (RR 783 ms), clear upright P waves in II/aVF with PR 148 ms. QRS 66 ms, axis +60 degrees = normal, no bundle branch block. QT about 380 ms, QTc about 425 ms. The prior tracing 109048192 (2020-02-02) was also sinus (with one interpolated premature beat producing an apparently irregular RR sequence) but had a long, low-amplitude, late T wave giving QT about 480 ms and QTc about 520 ms; QTc has fallen by roughly 95 ms, so QTC_DECREASE_60 is flagged. No change in rhythm or conduction.

Sinus tachycardia at 121 bpm, RR very regular (494-504 ms). One upright P per QRS in II/III/aVF, with the P onset partly merged into the preceding T wave; PR about 200 ms (upper limit of normal, not called first-degree AV block). QRS 84 ms, axis +46 degrees = normal, no bundle branch block. QT about 290 ms, QTc about 397 ms. Prior tracing 106186980 (2016-09-16, sinus 108 bpm, PR 168 ms, QRS 84 ms, QTc 394 ms): no rhythm, conduction or QTc change.

Sinus tachycardia at 101 bpm, regular (RR 592 ms), upright P in II/aVF with PR 142 ms. QRS 84 ms, axis +51 degrees = normal, no bundle branch block. QT about 312 ms, QTc 402 ms. The prior tracing 102910502 was recorded 34 seconds earlier the same morning and is essentially identical (sinus 101 bpm, PR 140 ms, QRS 82 ms, QTc 401 ms) - no changes.

Sinus bradycardia at 58 bpm; RR drifts smoothly from 1100 to 975 ms and a low-amplitude but consistent upright P precedes every QRS in II/III/aVF (peak about 200 ms before the QRS), PR about 190 ms. QRS 84 ms, axis +33 degrees = normal, no bundle branch block. Marked repolarisation prolongation: QT about 554 ms, Bazett QTc about 540 ms, on amiodarone (see the QT_SAFETY item). The prior tracing 100867733 (2022-04-06) showed atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response (mean 131 bpm, RR 324-616 ms, no P waves, QTc 434 ms), so sinus rhythm has been restored (RESOLVED_AF) and QTc has risen by about 106 ms (QTC_INCREASE_60).

Sinus tachycardia at 107 bpm, RR very regular (554-564 ms). Broad, slightly notched upright P in II/III/aVF ending just before the QRS; PR about 180 ms. QRS 66 ms, axis +52 degrees = normal, no bundle branch block. QT about 326 ms, QTc about 430 ms. Prior tracing 107274479 (2019-07-27, sinus 75 bpm, PR 150 ms, QRS 66 ms, QTc 411 ms): faster rate only, no rhythm, conduction or QTc change.

Regular narrow-complex tachycardia at 141 bpm (RR 404-454 ms, CV 0.02). Two low-amplitude atrial waves of identical inferior vector (positive II/III/aVF, negative I, positive V1) recur every 210-215 ms - one in the early ST segment about 85 ms after the QRS and one about 155 ms before the next QRS - giving an atrial rate near 280/min with 2:1 conduction, i.e. atrial flutter rather than sinus tachycardia; there is no isoelectric baseline and no PR interval can be measured, so pr_ms is null. The atrial wave vector also differs from this patient's documented sinus P wave (ECG 105224815, 2022-07-08). QRS 80 ms, axis 0 degrees = normal, no bundle branch block; QT about 274 ms, QTc about 420 ms. The prior tracing 109839112 (2022-07-11) showed atrial fibrillation (mean 110 bpm, RR 380-822 ms, no organised atrial activity, QTc 428 ms), so the rhythm has organised into flutter: NEW_ATRIAL_FLUTTER and RESOLVED_AF. Atrial flutter documented in the problem list (Condition I48.92) supports this reading; a pacemaker is present but the rhythm is not paced.

Sinus rhythm at 91 bpm, regular (RR 660 ms), upright P in II/aVF with negative component in V1; PR about 140 ms. QRS 76 ms, no bundle branch block. Frontal axis -39 degrees (net QRS positive in I, negative in II and aVF) = left axis deviation. QT about 334 ms, QTc 411 ms. Prior tracing 102616671 (2021-05-16, sinus 87 bpm, PR 134 ms, QRS 78 ms, QTc 393 ms, axis +20 degrees): no rhythm, conduction or QTc change (axis has shifted leftward, which is not a tracked change).

Sinus tachycardia at 112 bpm, RR extremely regular (536-540 ms), with a single well-formed upright P in II/III/aVF (biphasic in V1) before each QRS; PR 154 ms. Despite the documented history of atrial flutter, the atrial activity here is a single discrete P per QRS at a fixed PR, not flutter. QRS 88 ms, axis +31 degrees = normal, no bundle branch block. QT about 292 ms, QTc 398 ms. Prior tracing 102955795 (2022-07-04, sinus 115 bpm, PR 162 ms, QRS 88 ms, QTc 392 ms): unchanged.

Only ECG in the chart - no prior tracing. He is anticoagulated with warfarin.

interpretations.explanation: Sinus bradycardia at 53 bpm, RR regular (1092-1176 ms). Upright P before every QRS in II/aVF, PR 164 ms. Narrow QRS 84 ms with no bundle branch pattern; frontal axis -14 degrees (net QRS positive in I, slightly negative in aVF) = normal. QT 376 ms, Bazett QTc 353 ms at RR 1136 ms. Versus the prior tracing 108651109 (2018-12-13, sinus 66 bpm, PR 186 ms, QRS 88 ms, QTc 381 ms): rate slower, no rhythm, conduction or QTc change (QTc -28 ms).

Sinus rhythm at 68 bpm, regular (RR 880 ms). Upright P in II/aVF with a deep negative component in V1, PR about 135 ms. QRS 82 ms, axis +38 degrees = normal, no bundle branch block. Repolarisation is markedly prolonged with a broad late T wave: QT about 475 ms, Bazett QTc about 505 ms - at the QT watch-list threshold on escitalopram (separate QT_SAFETY item). Prior tracing 100065910 (2022-11-23, sinus 74 bpm, PR 120 ms, QRS 82 ms, QTc 354 ms): QTc has risen about 150 ms, so QTC_INCREASE_60 is flagged; rhythm and conduction unchanged.

Sinus rhythm at 70 bpm (RR 850 ms, minor sinus variation). Low-amplitude upright P in II/aVF before each QRS, PR about 155 ms. QRS 90 ms, axis +39 degrees = normal, no bundle branch block. Long, flat, low-amplitude T wave with QT about 484 ms and Bazett QTc about 523 ms on citalopram 40 mg daily (separate QT_SAFETY item). Prior tracing 107149156 (2020-06-17, sinus tachycardia 132 bpm, QRS 84 ms, QTc 404 ms): QTc up about 119 ms, so QTC_INCREASE_60; rhythm and conduction unchanged.

Sinus tachycardia at 121 bpm, RR regular (496 ms), with a small upright P in II/aVF before each QRS, PR about 130 ms. QRS 72 ms, axis +63 degrees = normal, no bundle branch block. QT about 282 ms, Bazett QTc about 400 ms. This is the only ECG in the chart, so there is no prior tracing for comparison.

Sinus tachycardia at 110 bpm; RR shortens smoothly from 570 to 540 ms. Small upright P in II/aVF (peak about 130 ms before the QRS) with PR about 120 ms and some PR-segment depression. QRS 82 ms, axis +45 degrees = normal, no bundle branch block. QT about 328 ms, Bazett QTc about 443 ms. Only ECG in the chart - no prior tracing.

Sinus rhythm at 97 bpm, regular (RR 616 ms). Prominent upright P in II/III/aVF, negative in V1, ending just before the QRS; PR about 118 ms. QRS 68 ms with tall R in V5 and net QRS positive in I and isoelectric in aVF: frontal axis about 0 degrees = normal. No bundle branch block. QT about 304 ms, QTc 387 ms. Only ECG in the chart - no prior tracing.

Sinus rhythm at 61 bpm (RR 984 ms after the first two longer cycles). Upright P in II/aVF peaking about 240 ms before the QRS with P onset about 275 ms and QRS onset about 60 ms before the R peak: PR about 212 ms, i.e. first-degree AV block. QRS is broad at 126 ms with a wide monophasic R in I and V6 peaking late and a deep broad QS in V1-V2 - left bundle branch block. Frontal axis -23 degrees = normal (borderline leftward). QT about 430 ms, QTc 433 ms. Prior tracing 103686933 (2024-06-03) shows the same LBBB (QRS 126 ms), PR about 208 ms and QTc 442 ms, so there is no new bundle branch block and no QTc change.

Atrial fibrillation with a mean ventricular rate of 99 bpm: RR intervals are chaotically irregular (386-1070 ms, coefficient of variation 0.29) and the averaged beat shows no organised P wave (peak pre-QRS amplitude only 0.01 mV in lead II), so no PR interval is measurable. QRS 74 ms, no bundle branch block. Frontal axis -63 degrees (QRS positive in I, negative in II and aVF) = left axis deviation. QT about 312 ms, Bazett QTc about 401 ms. Only ECG in the chart - no prior tracing. He is anticoagulated with warfarin.

Sinus rhythm at 77 bpm, regular (RR 783 ms), clear upright P waves in II/aVF with PR 148 ms. QRS 66 ms, axis +60 degrees = normal, no bundle branch block. QT about 380 ms, QTc about 425 ms. The prior tracing 109048192 (2020-02-02) was also sinus (with one interpolated premature beat producing an apparently irregular RR sequence) but had a long, low-amplitude, late T wave giving QT about 480 ms and QTc about 520 ms; QTc has fallen by roughly 95 ms, so QTC_DECREASE_60 is flagged. No change in rhythm or conduction.

Sinus tachycardia at 121 bpm, RR very regular (494-504 ms). One upright P per QRS in II/III/aVF, with the P onset partly merged into the preceding T wave; PR about 200 ms (upper limit of normal, not called first-degree AV block). QRS 84 ms, axis +46 degrees = normal, no bundle branch block. QT about 290 ms, QTc about 397 ms. Prior tracing 106186980 (2016-09-16, sinus 108 bpm, PR 168 ms, QRS 84 ms, QTc 394 ms): no rhythm, conduction or QTc change.

Sinus tachycardia at 101 bpm, regular (RR 592 ms), upright P in II/aVF with PR 142 ms. QRS 84 ms, axis +51 degrees = normal, no bundle branch block. QT about 312 ms, QTc 402 ms. The prior tracing 102910502 was recorded 34 seconds earlier the same morning and is essentially identical (sinus 101 bpm, PR 140 ms, QRS 82 ms, QTc 401 ms) - no changes.

Sinus bradycardia at 58 bpm; RR drifts smoothly from 1100 to 975 ms and a low-amplitude but consistent upright P precedes every QRS in II/III/aVF (peak about 200 ms before the QRS), PR about 190 ms. QRS 84 ms, axis +33 degrees = normal, no bundle branch block. Marked repolarisation prolongation: QT about 554 ms, Bazett QTc about 540 ms, on amiodarone (see the QT_SAFETY item). The prior tracing 100867733 (2022-04-06) showed atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response (mean 131 bpm, RR 324-616 ms, no P waves, QTc 434 ms), so sinus rhythm has been restored (RESOLVED_AF) and QTc has risen by about 106 ms (QTC_INCREASE_60).

Sinus tachycardia at 107 bpm, RR very regular (554-564 ms). Broad, slightly notched upright P in II/III/aVF ending just before the QRS; PR about 180 ms. QRS 66 ms, axis +52 degrees = normal, no bundle branch block. QT about 326 ms, QTc about 430 ms. Prior tracing 107274479 (2019-07-27, sinus 75 bpm, PR 150 ms, QRS 66 ms, QTc 411 ms): faster rate only, no rhythm, conduction or QTc change.

Regular narrow-complex tachycardia at 141 bpm (RR 404-454 ms, CV 0.02). Two low-amplitude atrial waves of identical inferior vector (positive II/III/aVF, negative I, positive V1) recur every 210-215 ms - one in the early ST segment about 85 ms after the QRS and one about 155 ms before the next QRS - giving an atrial rate near 280/min with 2:1 conduction, i.e. atrial flutter rather than sinus tachycardia; there is no isoelectric baseline and no PR interval can be measured, so pr_ms is null. The atrial wave vector also differs from this patient's documented sinus P wave (ECG 105224815, 2022-07-08). QRS 80 ms, axis 0 degrees = normal, no bundle branch block; QT about 274 ms, QTc about 420 ms. The prior tracing 109839112 (2022-07-11) showed atrial fibrillation (mean 110 bpm, RR 380-822 ms, no organised atrial activity, QTc 428 ms), so the rhythm has organised into flutter: NEW_ATRIAL_FLUTTER and RESOLVED_AF. Atrial flutter documented in the problem list (Condition I48.92) supports this reading; a pacemaker is present but the rhythm is not paced.

Sinus rhythm at 91 bpm, regular (RR 660 ms), upright P in II/aVF with negative component in V1; PR about 140 ms. QRS 76 ms, no bundle branch block. Frontal axis -39 degrees (net QRS positive in I, negative in II and aVF) = left axis deviation. QT about 334 ms, QTc 411 ms. Prior tracing 102616671 (2021-05-16, sinus 87 bpm, PR 134 ms, QRS 78 ms, QTc 393 ms, axis +20 degrees): no rhythm, conduction or QTc change (axis has shifted leftward, which is not a tracked change).

Sinus tachycardia at 112 bpm, RR extremely regular (536-540 ms), with a single well-formed upright P in II/III/aVF (biphasic in V1) before each QRS; PR 154 ms. Despite the documented history of atrial flutter, the atrial activity here is a single discrete P per QRS at a fixed PR, not flutter. QRS 88 ms, axis +31 degrees = normal, no bundle branch block. QT about 292 ms, QTc 398 ms. Prior tracing 102955795 (2022-07-04, sinus 115 bpm, PR 162 ms, QRS 88 ms, QTc 392 ms): unchanged.

interpretations.explanation: Sinus bradycardia at 53 bpm, RR regular (1092-1176 ms). Upright P before every QRS in II/aVF, PR 164 ms. Narrow QRS 84 ms with no bundle branch pattern; frontal axis -14 degrees (net QRS positive in I, slightly negative in aVF) = normal. QT 376 ms, Bazett QTc 353 ms at RR 1136 ms. Versus the prior tracing 108651109 (2018-12-13, sinus 66 bpm, PR 186 ms, QRS 88 ms, QTc 381 ms): rate slower, no rhythm, conduction or QTc change (QTc -28 ms).

Sinus rhythm at 68 bpm, regular (RR 880 ms). Upright P in II/aVF with a deep negative component in V1, PR about 135 ms. QRS 82 ms, axis +38 degrees = normal, no bundle branch block. Repolarisation is markedly prolonged with a broad late T wave: QT about 475 ms, Bazett QTc about 505 ms - at the QT watch-list threshold on escitalopram (separate QT_SAFETY item). Prior tracing 100065910 (2022-11-23, sinus 74 bpm, PR 120 ms, QRS 82 ms, QTc 354 ms): QTc has risen about 150 ms, so QTC_INCREASE_60 is flagged; rhythm and conduction unchanged.

Sinus rhythm at 70 bpm (RR 850 ms, minor sinus variation). Low-amplitude upright P in II/aVF before each QRS, PR about 155 ms. QRS 90 ms, axis +39 degrees = normal, no bundle branch block. Long, flat, low-amplitude T wave with QT about 484 ms and Bazett QTc about 523 ms on citalopram 40 mg daily (separate QT_SAFETY item). Prior tracing 107149156 (2020-06-17, sinus tachycardia 132 bpm, QRS 84 ms, QTc 404 ms): QTc up about 119 ms, so QTC_INCREASE_60; rhythm and conduction unchanged.

Sinus tachycardia at 121 bpm, RR regular (496 ms), with a small upright P in II/aVF before each QRS, PR about 130 ms. QRS 72 ms, axis +63 degrees = normal, no bundle branch block. QT about 282 ms, Bazett QTc about 400 ms. This is the only ECG in the chart, so there is no prior tracing for comparison.

Sinus tachycardia at 110 bpm; RR shortens smoothly from 570 to 540 ms. Small upright P in II/aVF (peak about 130 ms before the QRS) with PR about 120 ms and some PR-segment depression. QRS 82 ms, axis +45 degrees = normal, no bundle branch block. QT about 328 ms, Bazett QTc about 443 ms. Only ECG in the chart - no prior tracing.

Sinus rhythm at 97 bpm, regular (RR 616 ms). Prominent upright P in II/III/aVF, negative in V1, ending just before the QRS; PR about 118 ms. QRS 68 ms with tall R in V5 and net QRS positive in I and isoelectric in aVF: frontal axis about 0 degrees = normal. No bundle branch block. QT about 304 ms, QTc 387 ms. Only ECG in the chart - no prior tracing.

Sinus rhythm at 61 bpm (RR 984 ms after the first two longer cycles). Upright P in II/aVF peaking about 240 ms before the QRS with P onset about 275 ms and QRS onset about 60 ms before the R peak: PR about 212 ms, i.e. first-degree AV block. QRS is broad at 126 ms with a wide monophasic R in I and V6 peaking late and a deep broad QS in V1-V2 - left bundle branch block. Frontal axis -23 degrees = normal (borderline leftward). QT about 430 ms, QTc 433 ms. Prior tracing 103686933 (2024-06-03) shows the same LBBB (QRS 126 ms), PR about 208 ms and QTc 442 ms, so there is no new bundle branch block and no QTc change.

Atrial fibrillation with a mean ventricular rate of 99 bpm: RR intervals are chaotically irregular (386-1070 ms, coefficient of variation 0.29) and the averaged beat shows no organised P wave (peak pre-QRS amplitude only 0.01 mV in lead II), so no PR interval is measurable. QRS 74 ms, no bundle branch block. Frontal axis -63 degrees (QRS positive in I, negative in II and aVF) = left axis deviation. QT about 312 ms, Bazett QTc about 401 ms. Only ECG in the chart - no prior tracing. He is anticoagulated with warfarin.

Sinus bradycardia at 52 bpm, RR very regular (1160 ms), with a low-amplitude upright P in II/aVF and PR about 166 ms. QRS 86 ms, axis +34 degrees = normal, no bundle branch block. Tall T waves; QT about 404 ms, Bazett QTc 375 ms. Prior tracing 104629882 (2023-05-22) was also sinus at 57 bpm with a single premature beat and compensatory pause (QTc 345 ms), so no rhythm, conduction or QTc change.

Atrial fibrillation with a slow, irregular ventricular response, mean rate 53 bpm: RR intervals vary from 696 to 1164 ms with no repeating pattern and the averaged beat has essentially no atrial deflection (0.04 mV in lead II, versus 0.34 mV on the previous tracing), so no PR interval can be measured. QRS 82 ms, axis +25 degrees = normal, no bundle branch block. QT about 416 ms, Bazett QTc 392 ms. The prior tracing 107873952 (2024-11-12) was sinus rhythm at 69 bpm with a clear P wave and PR 166 ms (QTc 388 ms), so this is NEW_AF. She is anticoagulated with apixaban.

Sinus rhythm at 77 bpm, regular (RR 783 ms), clear upright P waves in II/aVF with PR 148 ms. QRS 66 ms, axis +60 degrees = normal, no bundle branch block. QT about 380 ms, QTc about 425 ms. The prior tracing 109048192 (2020-02-02) was also sinus (with one interpolated premature beat producing an apparently irregular RR sequence) but had a long, low-amplitude, late T wave giving QT about 480 ms and QTc about 520 ms; QTc has fallen by roughly 95 ms, so QTC_DECREASE_60 is flagged. No change in rhythm or conduction.

Sinus tachycardia at 121 bpm, RR very regular (494-504 ms). One upright P per QRS in II/III/aVF, with the P onset partly merged into the preceding T wave; PR about 200 ms (upper limit of normal, not called first-degree AV block). QRS 84 ms, axis +46 degrees = normal, no bundle branch block. QT about 290 ms, QTc about 397 ms. Prior tracing 106186980 (2016-09-16, sinus 108 bpm, PR 168 ms, QRS 84 ms, QTc 394 ms): no rhythm, conduction or QTc change.

Sinus tachycardia at 101 bpm, regular (RR 592 ms), upright P in II/aVF with PR 142 ms. QRS 84 ms, axis +51 degrees = normal, no bundle branch block. QT about 312 ms, QTc 402 ms. The prior tracing 102910502 was recorded 34 seconds earlier the same morning and is essentially identical (sinus 101 bpm, PR 140 ms, QRS 82 ms, QTc 401 ms) - no changes.

Sinus bradycardia at 58 bpm; RR drifts smoothly from 1100 to 975 ms and a low-amplitude but consistent upright P precedes every QRS in II/III/aVF (peak about 200 ms before the QRS), PR about 190 ms. QRS 84 ms, axis +33 degrees = normal, no bundle branch block. Marked repolarisation prolongation: QT about 554 ms, Bazett QTc about 540 ms, on amiodarone (see the QT_SAFETY item). The prior tracing 100867733 (2022-04-06) showed atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response (mean 131 bpm, RR 324-616 ms, no P waves, QTc 434 ms), so sinus rhythm has been restored (RESOLVED_AF) and QTc has risen by about 106 ms (QTC_INCREASE_60).

Sinus tachycardia at 107 bpm, RR very regular (554-564 ms). Broad, slightly notched upright P in II/III/aVF ending just before the QRS; PR about 180 ms. QRS 66 ms, axis +52 degrees = normal, no bundle branch block. QT about 326 ms, QTc about 430 ms. Prior tracing 107274479 (2019-07-27, sinus 75 bpm, PR 150 ms, QRS 66 ms, QTc 411 ms): faster rate only, no rhythm, conduction or QTc change.

Regular narrow-complex tachycardia at 141 bpm (RR 404-454 ms, CV 0.02). Two low-amplitude atrial waves of identical inferior vector (positive II/III/aVF, negative I, positive V1) recur every 210-215 ms - one in the early ST segment about 85 ms after the QRS and one about 155 ms before the next QRS - giving an atrial rate near 280/min with 2:1 conduction, i.e. atrial flutter rather than sinus tachycardia; there is no isoelectric baseline and no PR interval can be measured, so pr_ms is null. The atrial wave vector also differs from this patient's documented sinus P wave (ECG 105224815, 2022-07-08). QRS 80 ms, axis 0 degrees = normal, no bundle branch block; QT about 274 ms, QTc about 420 ms. The prior tracing 109839112 (2022-07-11) showed atrial fibrillation (mean 110 bpm, RR 380-822 ms, no organised atrial activity, QTc 428 ms), so the rhythm has organised into flutter: NEW_ATRIAL_FLUTTER and RESOLVED_AF. Atrial flutter documented in the problem list (Condition I48.92) supports this reading; a pacemaker is present but the rhythm is not paced.

Sinus rhythm at 91 bpm, regular (RR 660 ms), upright P in II/aVF with negative component in V1; PR about 140 ms. QRS 76 ms, no bundle branch block. Frontal axis -39 degrees (net QRS positive in I, negative in II and aVF) = left axis deviation. QT about 334 ms, QTc 411 ms. Prior tracing 102616671 (2021-05-16, sinus 87 bpm, PR 134 ms, QRS 78 ms, QTc 393 ms, axis +20 degrees): no rhythm, conduction or QTc change (axis has shifted leftward, which is not a tracked change).

Sinus tachycardia at 112 bpm, RR extremely regular (536-540 ms), with a single well-formed upright P in II/III/aVF (biphasic in V1) before each QRS; PR 154 ms. Despite the documented history of atrial flutter, the atrial activity here is a single discrete P per QRS at a fixed PR, not flutter. QRS 88 ms, axis +31 degrees = normal, no bundle branch block. QT about 292 ms, QTc 398 ms. Prior tracing 102955795 (2022-07-04, sinus 115 bpm, PR 162 ms, QRS 88 ms, QTc 392 ms): unchanged.

arguments.explanation: Sinus tachycardia at 121 bpm, RR very regular (494 ms), with an upright P in I/II before each QRS and PR about 130 ms. interpretations.explanation: Sinus bradycardia at 53 bpm, RR regular (1092-1176 ms). Upright P before every QRS in II/aVF, PR 164 ms. Versus the prior tracing 108651109 (2018-12-13, sinus 66 bpm, PR 186 ms, QRS 88 ms, QTc 381 ms): rate slower, no rhythm, conduction or QTc change (QTc -28 ms).

Prior tracing 100065910 (2022-11-23, sinus 74 bpm, PR 120 ms, QRS 82 ms, QTc 354 ms): QTc has risen about 150 ms, so QTC_INCREASE_60 is flagged; rhythm and conduction unchanged.

Sinus rhythm at 70 bpm (RR 850 ms, minor sinus variation). Low-amplitude upright P in II/aVF before each QRS, PR about 155 ms. QRS 90 ms, axis +39 degrees = normal, no bundle branch block. Prior tracing 107149156 (2020-06-17, sinus tachycardia 132 bpm, QRS 84 ms, QTc 404 ms): QTc up about 119 ms, so QTC_INCREASE_60; rhythm and conduction unchanged.

Sinus tachycardia at 121 bpm, RR regular (496 ms), with a small upright P in II/aVF before each QRS, PR about 130 ms. QRS 72 ms, axis +63 degrees = normal, no bundle branch block. Sinus rhythm at 61 bpm (RR 984 ms after the first two longer cycles). Upright P in II/aVF peaking about 240 ms before the QRS with P onset about 275 ms and QRS onset about 60 ms before the R peak: PR about 212 ms, i.e. first-degree AV block. QT about 430 ms, QTc 433 ms. Prior tracing 103686933 (2024-06-03) shows the same LBBB (QRS 126 ms), PR about 208 ms and QTc 442 ms, so there is no new bundle branch block and no QTc change.

Atrial fibrillation with a mean ventricular rate of 99 bpm: RR intervals are chaotically irregular (386-1070 ms, coefficient of variation 0.29) and the averaged beat shows no organised P wave (peak pre-QRS amplitude only 0.01 mV in lead II), so no PR interval is measurable. QRS 74 ms, no bundle branch block. Frontal axis -63 degrees (QRS positive in I, negative in II and aVF) = left axis deviation. QT about 312 ms, Bazett QTc about 401 ms. Only ECG in the chart - no prior tracing. He is anticoagulated with warfarin.

Sinus bradycardia at 52 bpm, RR very regular (1160 ms), with a low-amplitude upright P in II/aVF and PR about 166 ms. QRS 86 ms, axis +34 degrees = normal, no bundle branch block. Prior tracing 104629882 (2023-05-22) was also sinus at 57 bpm with a single premature beat and compensatory pause (QTc 345 ms), so no rhythm, conduction or QTc change.

Atrial fibrillation with a slow, irregular ventricular response, mean rate 53 bpm: RR intervals vary from 696 to 1164 ms with no repeating pattern and the averaged beat has essentially no atrial deflection (0.04 mV in lead II, versus 0.34 mV on the previous tracing), so no PR interval can be measured. Regular narrow-complex tachycardia at 141 bpm (RR 404-454 ms, CV 0.02). Two low-amplitude atrial waves of identical inferior vector (positive II/III/aVF, negative I, positive V1) recur every 210-215 ms - one in the early ST segment about 85 ms after the QRS and one about 155 ms before the next QRS - giving an atrial rate near 280/min with 2:1 conduction, i.e. atrial flutter rather than sinus tachycardia; there is no isoelectric baseline and no PR interval can be measured, so pr_ms is null. The atrial wave vector also differs from this patient's documented sinus P wave (ECG 105224815, 2022-07-08). QRS 80 ms, axis 0 degrees = normal, no bundle branch block; QT about 274 ms, QTc about 420 ms. The prior tracing 109839112 (2022-07-11) showed atrial fibrillation (mean 110 bpm, RR 380-822 ms, no organised atrial activity, QTc 428 ms), so the rhythm has organised into flutter: NEW_ATRIAL_FLUTTER and RESOLVED_AF. Atrial flutter documented in the problem list (Condition I48.92) supports this reading; a pacemaker is present but the rhythm is not paced.

Prior tracing 102616671 (2021-05-16, sinus 87 bpm, PR 134 ms, QRS 78 ms, QTc 393 ms, axis +20 degrees): no rhythm, conduction or QTc change (axis has shifted leftward, which is not a tracked change).

Sinus tachycardia at 112 bpm, RR extremely regular (536-540 ms), with a single well-formed upright P in II/III/aVF (biphasic in V1) before each QRS; PR 154 ms. Despite the documented history of atrial flutter, the atrial activity here is a single discrete P per QRS at a fixed PR, not flutter. QRS 88 ms, axis +31 degrees = normal, no bundle branch block. QT about 292 ms, QTc 398 ms. Prior tracing 102955795 (2022-07-04, sinus 115 bpm, PR 162 ms, QRS 88 ms, QTc 392 ms): unchanged.

Prior tracing 100065910 (2022-11-23, sinus 74 bpm, PR 120 ms, QRS 82 ms, QTc 354 ms): QTc has risen about 150 ms, so QTC_INCREASE_60 is flagged; rhythm and conduction unchanged.

Sinus rhythm at 97 bpm, regular (RR 616 ms). Prominent upright P in II/III/aVF, negative in V1, ending just before the QRS; PR about 118 ms. Only ECG in the chart - no prior tracing.

Sinus rhythm at 61 bpm (RR 984 ms after the first two longer cycles). Upright P in II/aVF peaking about 240 ms before the QRS with P onset about 275 ms and QRS onset about 60 ms before the R peak: PR about 212 ms, i.e. first-degree AV block. QRS is broad at 126 ms with a wide monophasic R in I and V6 peaking late and a deep broad QS in V1-V2 - left bundle branch block. Frontal axis -23 degrees = normal (borderline leftward). QT about 430 ms, QTc 433 ms. Prior tracing 103686933 (2024-06-03) shows the same LBBB (QRS 126 ms), PR about 208 ms and QTc 442 ms, so there is no new bundle branch block and no QTc change.

Atrial fibrillation with a mean ventricular rate of 99 bpm: RR intervals are chaotically irregular (386-1070 ms, coefficient of variation 0.29) and the averaged beat shows no organised P wave (peak pre-QRS amplitude only 0.01 mV in lead II), so no PR interval is measurable. QRS 74 ms, no bundle branch block. Frontal axis -63 degrees (QRS positive in I, negative in II and aVF) = left axis deviation. QT about 312 ms, Bazett QTc about 401 ms. Only ECG in the chart - no prior tracing. He is anticoagulated with warfarin.

Sinus bradycardia at 52 bpm, RR very regular (1160 ms), with a low-amplitude upright P in II/aVF and PR about 166 ms. QRS 86 ms, axis +34 degrees = normal, no bundle branch block. Atrial fibrillation with a slow, irregular ventricular response, mean rate 53 bpm: RR intervals vary from 696 to 1164 ms with no repeating pattern and the averaged beat has essentially no atrial deflection (0.04 mV in lead II, versus 0.34 mV on the previous tracing), so no PR interval can be measured. Sinus tachycardia at 121 bpm, RR very regular (494 ms), with an upright P in I/II before each QRS and PR about 130 ms. The QRS is now narrow at 84 ms with no terminal R in V1; frontal axis +139 degrees (net QRS negative in I, positive in aVF) = right axis deviation. QT about 292 ms, Bazett QTc about 418 ms. Regular narrow-complex tachycardia at 141 bpm (RR 404-454 ms, CV 0.02). Two low-amplitude atrial waves of identical inferior vector (positive II/III/aVF, negative I, positive V1) recur every 210-215 ms - one in the early ST segment about 85 ms after the QRS and one about 155 ms before the next QRS - giving an atrial rate near 280/min with 2:1 conduction, i.e. atrial flutter rather than sinus tachycardia; there is no isoelectric baseline and no PR interval can be measured, so pr_ms is null. The atrial wave vector also differs from this patient's documented sinus P wave (ECG 105224815, 2022-07-08). QRS 80 ms, axis 0 degrees = normal, no bundle branch block; QT about 274 ms, QTc about 420 ms. The prior tracing 109839112 (2022-07-11) showed atrial fibrillation (mean 110 bpm, RR 380-822 ms, no organised atrial activity, QTc 428 ms), so the rhythm has organised into flutter: NEW_ATRIAL_FLUTTER and RESOLVED_AF. Atrial flutter documented in the problem list (Condition I48.92) supports this reading; a pacemaker is present but the rhythm is not paced.

Prior tracing 100065910 (2022-11-23, sinus 74 bpm, PR 120 ms, QRS 82 ms, QTc 354 ms): QTc has risen about 150 ms, so QTC_INCREASE_60 is flagged; rhythm and conduction unchanged.

Sinus rhythm at 61 bpm (RR 984 ms after the first two longer cycles). QT about 430 ms, QTc 433 ms. Prior tracing 103686933 (2024-06-03) shows the same LBBB (QRS 126 ms), PR about 208 ms and QTc 442 ms, so there is no new bundle branch block and no QTc change.

Atrial fibrillation with a mean ventricular rate of 99 bpm: RR intervals are chaotically irregular (386-1070 ms, coefficient of variation 0.29) and the averaged beat shows no organised P wave (peak pre-QRS amplitude only 0.01 mV in lead II), so no PR interval is measurable. Sinus bradycardia at 52 bpm, RR very regular (1160 ms), with a low-amplitude upright P in II/aVF and PR about 166 ms. QRS 86 ms, axis +34 degrees = normal, no bundle branch block. Sinus rhythm at 77 bpm, regular (RR 783 ms), clear upright P waves in II/aVF with PR 148 ms. QRS 66 ms, axis +60 degrees = normal, no bundle branch block. QT about 380 ms, QTc about 425 ms. Prior tracing 107274479 (2019-07-27, sinus 75 bpm, PR 150 ms, QRS 66 ms, QTc 411 ms): faster rate only, no rhythm, conduction or QTc change.

Regular narrow-complex tachycardia at 141 bpm (RR 404-454 ms, CV 0.02). Two low-amplitude atrial waves of identical inferior vector (positive II/III/aVF, negative I, positive V1) recur every 210-215 ms - one in the early ST segment about 85 ms after the QRS and one about 155 ms before the next QRS - giving an atrial rate near 280/min with 2:1 conduction, i.e. atrial flutter rather than sinus tachycardia; there is no isoelectric baseline and no PR interval can be measured, so pr_ms is null. The atrial wave vector also differs from this patient's documented sinus P wave (ECG 105224815, 2022-07-08). QRS 80 ms, axis 0 degrees = normal, no bundle branch block; QT about 274 ms, QTc about 420 ms. The prior tracing 109839112 (2022-07-11) showed atrial fibrillation (mean 110 bpm, RR 380-822 ms, no organised atrial activity, QTc 428 ms), so the rhythm has organised into flutter: NEW_ATRIAL_FLUTTER and RESOLVED_AF. Atrial flutter documented in the problem list (Condition I48.92) supports this reading; a pacemaker is present but the rhythm is not paced.

Sinus tachycardia at 112 bpm, RR extremely regular (536-540 ms), with a single well-formed upright P in II/III/aVF (biphasic in V1) before each QRS; PR 154 ms. Despite the documented history of atrial flutter, the atrial activity here is a single discrete P per QRS at a fixed PR, not flutter. QRS 88 ms, axis +31 degrees = normal, no bundle branch block. QT about 292 ms, QTc 398 ms. Prior tracing 102955795 (2022-07-04, sinus 115 bpm, PR 162 ms, QRS 88 ms, QTc 392 ms): unchanged.

Regular rhythm at 69 bpm (RR 872 ms) that is not sinus: the atrial wave preceding each QRS is inverted in II, III and aVF and upright in I and aVL (peak about 130 ms before the QRS), indicating a low/ectopic atrial or coronary-sinus focus rather than sinus node origin. QRS 76 ms with a very dominant R in I and aVL, no bundle branch block; net QRS area gives a frontal axis of about -25 degrees = normal (borderline leftward). QT about 392 ms, Bazett QTc about 420 ms. The prior tracing 104232242 (2025-04-27) showed the same non-sinus atrial activation at 60 bpm with QTc about 400 ms; no atrial fibrillation, flutter, paced rhythm, bundle branch block or QTc change.

QRS 80 ms, axis 0 degrees = normal, no bundle branch block; QT about 274 ms, QTc about 420 ms. The prior tracing 109839112 (2022-07-11) showed atrial fibrillation (mean 110 bpm, RR 380-822 ms, no organised atrial activity, QTc 428 ms), so the rhythm has organised into flutter: NEW_ATRIAL_FLUTTER and RESOLVED_AF. Sinus tachycardia at 102 bpm, RR regular (589 ms), upright P in II/aVF with PR about 134 ms. QRS 84 ms, axis +44 degrees = normal, no bundle branch block. QRS 88 ms, axis +22 degrees = normal, no bundle branch block. Widespread ST depression with a discrete T wave peaking at 190 ms that returns to baseline by about 275 ms: QT about 328 ms, Bazett QTc about 430 ms. No rhythm or conduction change.

Regular rhythm at 69 bpm (RR 872 ms) that is not sinus: the atrial wave preceding each QRS is inverted in II, III and aVF and upright in I and aVL (peak about 130 ms before the QRS), indicating a low/ectopic atrial or coronary-sinus focus rather than sinus node origin. Atrioventricular conduction is 1:1 with a fixed PR of about 145 ms. QRS 76 ms with a very dominant R in I and aVL, no bundle branch block; net QRS area gives a frontal axis of about -25 degrees = normal (borderline leftward). QT about 392 ms, Bazett QTc about 420 ms. The prior tracing 104232242 (2025-04-27) showed the same non-sinus atrial activation at 60 bpm with QTc about 400 ms; no atrial fibrillation, flutter, paced rhythm, bundle branch block or QTc change.

Sinus rhythm at 83 bpm, RR very regular (720 ms). Upright P in II/aVF with PR about 146 ms. Narrow QRS 62 ms, axis +53 degrees = normal, no bundle branch block. QT about 332 ms, Bazett QTc 391 ms. Only ECG in the chart - no prior tracing.

arguments.explanation: Sinus rhythm at 69 bpm, regular (RR 864 ms), with a consistent low-amplitude atrial deflection before each QRS and PR about 145 ms. QRS 86 ms, no bundle branch pattern. QT about 350 ms, Bazett QTc 377 ms. The limb leads are markedly discordant - deeply negative P, QRS and T in leads I and II with positive deflections in III - which is the pattern of right/left arm electrode reversal; with the recording taken at face value the net QRS area gives a frontal axis of about -171 degrees, but after correcting for the probable arm-lead reversal the axis is normal, and that is what is reported here. Only ECG in the chart - no prior tracing.

Her most recent ECG (102298909, 2025-03-14) shows sinus rhythm, which does not remove the indication in paroxysmal AF. Bleeding risk (thrombocytopenia, history of falls, non-ruptured cerebral aneurysm) should be weighed at review.

Continuation needs prescriber review.

The 2026-07-15 cardiology note states the intent was to switch from rivaroxaban to apixaban for insurance coverage, but the rivaroxaban order was never stopped, so both remain active at 2026-09-24. Overlapping anticoagulants carry a major bleeding risk and one order must be discontinued.

Both ECGs recorded that same day contradict it: 107914094 (2026-06-10 17:13) and 103088543 (2026-06-10 19:36) each show an irregularly irregular narrow-complex rhythm with no organised P waves at a mean ventricular rate of 139 and 144 bpm - atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response, not sinus rhythm at 72. Amiodarone 200 mg daily (watch-list drug) is currently ordered (MedicationRequest/c6f532e9, 2026-08-22 to 2027-01-05). arguments.explanation: Sinus rhythm at 69 bpm, regular (RR 864 ms), with a consistent low-amplitude atrial deflection before each QRS and PR about 145 ms. QRS 86 ms, no bundle branch pattern. QT about 350 ms, Bazett QTc 377 ms. As recorded, the net QRS area is strongly negative in lead I (-15.3 mV.ms) and slightly negative in aVF (-2.4 mV.ms), giving a frontal axis of about -171 degrees, i.e. extreme axis deviation, which is what is reported. Note however that the limb leads are markedly discordant - P, QRS and T all deeply negative in I and II with positive deflections in III and an upright QRS in aVR - while the precordial leads show normal R-wave progression; this is the pattern of right/left arm electrode reversal, and after correcting for it the frontal axis would be about -10 degrees (normal). Repeat with correct electrode placement is advised. Only ECG in the chart - no prior tracing.
